conventions.convention: A companion embedding preserves orientation and matches the product meridian and longitude with the positive meridian and preferred longitude. Winding number is the coefficient of the oriented core in integral homology.
Essential means incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. Atoroidal means every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel; it does not mean hyperbolic.
A JSJ system cuts into atoroidal or Seifert-fibered components; minimality is inclusion-minimality, rather than merely a chosen maximal torus family.

The finiteness bound assumes countable choice, a supplied finite whole-star triangulation compatible with the smooth structure, and no product cut component. The bound is uniform for that fixed triangulation.
The ball-compression lemma permits a topological two-sided torus and produces a topological disk under full AC. The cutting lemma instead explicitly concerns PL tori, PL spheres, and PL balls.
Smooth ambient vertical-or-horizontal normalization requires neat boundary embedding. Broader boundary-preimage embeddings receive a smooth embedding isotopy and a topological ambient extension.
Annulus verticalization may change the Seifert fibration only for the underlying orientable manifolds T²×I and the orientable twisted interval bundle over the Klein bottle.

load_bearing.statement: Defines compressing and boundary-compressing disks, incompressibility, essentiality, boundary-parallelity, irreducibility, atoroidality, Seifert fibrations, and inclusion-minimal JSJ systems. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

Assume full AC. Every chosen compact exterior of a smooth oriented knot has a finite inclusion-minimal collection of disjoint incompressible interior tori cutting it into atoroidal or Seifert-fibered components. Any two such inclusion-minimal collections are ambient isotopic. Atoroidal pieces are not asserted hyperbolic.

Under full AC, a connected two-sided essential neatly embedded annulus or torus in a compact connected irreducible Seifert-fibered three-manifold is ambient isotopic to a vertical or horizontal surface. A horizontal representative satisfies the displayed branched-cover Euler formula, and cutting along a two-sided horizontal surface gives an interval bundle. The broader boundary-preimage variant has the separately stated embedding and topological ambient conclusions.

Assume full AC. For a nontrivial smooth companion with specified companion solid torus, if the pattern exterior has incompressible outer torus and is not a product between its outer and inner tori, the companion torus is incompressible and not boundary-parallel in the satellite exterior, hence essential.

A connected two-sided properly embedded incompressible surface with nonempty boundary in a compact connected orientable irreducible three-manifold with torus boundary is either boundary-incompressible or a boundary-parallel annulus.

Under full AC and the stated nontrivial-companion, incompressible-outer-boundary and nonproduct-pattern hypotheses, if both companion-torus cut pieces are atoroidal or Seifert-fibered and the whole satellite exterior is neither, every inclusion-minimal JSJ system consists of one torus ambient isotopic to the companion torus.

seams_checked.note: Chosen tube, exterior, meridian, preferred longitude, and normal-frame interfaces match the satellite and JSJ uses. Results invoking the exterior machinery retain the relevant choice hypotheses.
The nontrivial-knot convention, smooth Schoenflies, relative transversality, finite PL Loop, and subcomplex-subdivision uses retain their stated categories and assumptions.
The cable example uses the trefoil presentation and peripheral formula with full AC. Its slopes are 2λ+μ and λ+6μ, with determinant −11. The diagram agrees with these markings.

The actual supplier used is knot-exterior irreducibility under countable choice. Full AC discharges that premise where required; no Khovanov detection conclusion is substituted for a geometric boundary theorem.
Consumers preserve embedded-torus atoroidality and separately require non-Seifert and other hyperbolization hypotheses. They do not infer hyperbolicity from the JSJ theorem alone.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its current listed item bodies contain no direct citation to an assigned batch-71 item; no strengthened JSJ or satellite proposition is asserted through this edge.

The enhanced-polynomial classification item cites JSJ Proof 1.1 for compactness, connectedness, and the single torus boundary. Satellite recognition, Seifert-knot recognition, and hyperbolization have separate suppliers; the citation does not overstate JSJ.
